question:
A 24 year-old-male comes to the office due to numbness on the dorsal aspect of the lateral three-and-a-half fingers, and weakness of extension at the wrist and fingers after receiving an intramuscular injection on his shoulder. 

Which of the following nerves is most likely damaged?
A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of chest pain. An ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, avF, V4, V5, and V6. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old male presents with large, painful, deep-seated pimples that are interconnected in multiple areas and often leave scars. They are most predominant on the chest, back, buttocks, and thighs and have grown gradually over the last couple of years. What is the correct diagnosis?

A 29-year-old female presents with a sudden onset of a red, painful rash on their chest, arms, and legs. The rash has evolved into blisters and ulcers, and the affected body surface area is less than 10%. The patient is also experiencing fever, sore throat, and conjunctivitis. What is the correct diagnosis?

A 32-year-old male presents to the clinic with symptoms of cough, weight loss, and fever for the past two months. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and scattered crackles in the left lung. A chest x-ray shows consolidation in the left lung. A sputum culture test is positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. What is the appropriate treatment?

answers.option: RIPE for 2 months, followed by rifampin + isoniazid for 4 months
Isoniazid + rifampin for 4 months followed RIPE for 2 months

question: A 45-year-old patient with a history of tobacco use and chronic stress presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and heartburn. Upper endoscopy reveals a peptic ulcer with H-pylori infection. What is the appropriate treatment regimen for this patient?

answers.option: Antacids as needed for symptom relief

question: A 35-year-old male patient with a fever and pleuritic chest pain present to the emergency department. His ECG shows diffuse ST elevations and PR depression. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A newborn baby is noted to have a flat facial profile, a single crease across the palm of the hand, and a gap between the first and second toes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man comes to the clinic with a fever, cough productive of green sputum, and difficulty breathing. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. He has no underlying lung conditions and has not traveled recently. A chest x-ray shows an area of consolidation in the right lower lobe. What is the best treatment choice for this patient?

A 65-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma receives CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) regimen as part of his chemotherapy treatment. Two weeks after completing the regimen, he develops hematuria and severe abdominal pain. What could have prevented this complication?

A 17-year-old boy presents with low-grade fever, cough, and difficulty breathing for the past week. He has associated fatigue and appears jaundiced. Liver function tests show an AST of 110 and an ALT of 95. A chest x-ray shows interstitial infiltrates. He has not traveled recently and has not been exposed to any known infectious sources. Which organism is most likely responsible?

A 27-year-old woman presents with intermittent palpitations and dizziness. Her EKG shows a fixed but prolonged PR interval and a dropped beat after every 2 QRS complexes. Which abnormal rhythm is this?

A 58-year-old male patient presents with progressive dysphagia to solid foods. He is eventually diagnosed with irresectable carcinoma of the lower third of the esophagus. Which of these feeding options is ideal for long-term in this patient?

A 32-year-old female presents with a high-grade fever and cough for the last 3 days. A chest X-ray reveals a lobar infiltrate with D-shaped opacity at the pleural region. Which complication has this patient developed?
Sputum culture from a patient suspected of having pneumonia shows gram-positive diplococci in chains. Which of these is the most likely pathogen?
Which of these is not part of the criteria for diagnosing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)?
What is the pathophysiology behind capillary leak in heart failure?

answers.option: Capillary oncotic pressure is greater than hydrostatic pressure
Capillary hydrostatic pressure is equal to oncotic pressure
Capillary oncotic pressure and hydrostatic pressure act in same direction
Capillary hydrostatic pressure is greater than oncotic pressure

question: A 52-year-old male patient presents with sharp chest pain for the last 2 hours. An EKG reveals ST elevations in the inferior wall leads, and the patient's vitals show a BP of 90/55mmHg and a heart rate of 45/min. What is the treatment of choice for this patient's bradycardia?

A 40-year-old female patient presents to the emergency department with a blood pressure of 200/120 mmHg and symptoms of headache and shortness of breath. The patient is otherwise stable and has no signs and symptoms of any systemic involvement. Fundoscopy is unremarkable. What is the appropriate diagnosis in this case?

A 26-year-old man comes to the office with complaints of fever, night sweats, and joint pains over the last 1 week. He also describes a burning sensation with urination. He is a milkman by profession and has not traveled outside the country ever. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of these drugs is contraindicated in tuberculosis?
Which one of these diagnostic tests is the gold standard for diagnosing Wilson disease?

A 22-year-old woman presents with an itchy, blistering rash on her neck for the past 2 days. On examination, there is a well-demarcated erythematous rash on her neck with multiple blisters. She says she tried on a new necklace from an antique shop some days ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman presents with symptoms of dry mouth and eyes, fatigue, and joint pain. She has a history of rheumatoid arthritis and has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain management. She works as a banker and has no other medical history. Which of these is the best way to diagnose her current symptoms?
Which one of these ECG findings is associated with pulmonary embolism?

answers.option: S wave, Q wave, and T wave inversion in lead III
S in lead I, Q wave and T wave inversion in lead III
S wave, Q wave, and T wave inversion in lead I
Q wave in lead I, S wave in lead III
T wave inversion in lead I, Q and S waves in lead III

question:
A 40-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with complaints of proximal muscle weakness and difficulty climbing stairs, getting up from a seated position, and raising her arms above her head. She reports no recent illness or injury and has no significant medical history. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications.
Physical examination reveals symmetric proximal muscle weakness, with 3/5 strength in both hip flexors and deltoid muscles. In addition to these findings, the patient also has a violaceous rash on her face and eyelids and a rash on her knuckles. Which of these diagnostic tests is useful for this patient?
Which of these antibodies are associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis?

A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea. She has had pubic hair growth but remains short in stature, and has a short webbed neck. Which of these diagnoses is the most plausible explanation for her amenorrhea?
Which of these differences is found in biopsy results of non-alcoholic and alcoholic hepatitis?

A 35-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of abdominal pain, bloating, and alternating constipation and diarrhea for the past 6 months. She reports that her symptoms are often triggered by stress and occur primarily in the evening. She says that the symptoms get better with defecation. The patient reports no blood in her stools and no fever. Her medical history is significant for anxiety and depression for which she is currently being treated with an SSRI. On physical examination, her abdomen is diffusely tender to palpation but non-distended, and there are no masses or hepatosplenomegaly. A stool sample is negative for occult blood. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of these is an indication for thrombolytic therapy in a patient with pulmonary embolism?
Which of these mineral deficiencies can develop in a patient receiving total parenteral nutrition (TPN) for 3 months?

A 22-year-old female presents to the emergency with acute onset shortness of breath for the last 2 hours. She is a known case of asthma. Her history reveals she was stable on inhaled steroids. Current vitals are blood pressure 110/65mmHg, pulse 120/min, and respiratory rate 26/min. Oxygen saturation is 89% and instant ABG results confirm type 2 respiratory failure with acidosis. There are decreased breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation. Which of these is the next best step in management?
Which one of these is the first-line therapy for new-onset asthma?

A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency department complaining of fatigue, nausea, and jaundice that started 2 weeks ago. He admits to occasional alcohol consumption but denies any injection drug use. His physical examination reveals jaundice and mild hepatomegaly. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and positive hepatitis B surface antigen and IgM core antibody. What is the best management option for this patient?
Which one of these is a good treatment option for hepatitis D co-infection with Hepatitis B?
Which one of these is the best pharmacological treatment for HOCM?
What is the best treatment option for acute gout?

A 52-year-old male, with a known case of chronic heart failure, presents to the emergency with worsening shortness of breath. On inspection, he is dyspneic at rest and O2 saturation is at 85%. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral interstitial infiltrates. What is the best immediate therapy for this patient?
Which of these types of gastric ulcers is most likely benign?
Which one of these pleural fluid analyses is consistent with empyema?

A 45-year-old male with a history of asthma presents to the emergency room with a two-week history of worsening shortness of breath, cough, and night sweats. Physical examination reveals diffuse wheezing and peripheral eosinophilia. A palpable, rash with nodules is also found on the shins. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fever with chills, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and nausea. She reports no history of recent travel or intravenous drug use. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and has marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Laboratory tests reveal an elevated white blood cell count and elevated liver enzymes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with uncontrolled hypertension. She reports no symptoms but her blood pressure is found to be consistently elevated in her recent visits. She has been on multiple anti-hypertensive medications without success. Laboratory tests reveal low plasma renin activity and high aldosterone levels. What is the next best investigation?

A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency department after participating in a strenuous outdoor workout on a hot and humid summer day. He reports feeling dizzy and weak and has a fever of 105.9°F. He is confused, has hot, dry skin, and a rapid heartbeat. The patient's rectal temperature is 40.6°C. What is the diagnosis?
Which one of these is the best treatment regimen for prophylaxis in spontaneous bacterial peritonitis?

A 65-year-old female presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of chest pain and shortness of breath. She reports no history of cardiac disease but mentions that her husband passed away 2 days back. An ECG and cardiac enzymes are normal, but an echocardiogram shows a reversible systolic dysfunction of the left ventricular apex. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation and previous DVT presents to the emergency department with a complaint of easy bruising and hematomas on his lower extremities. The patient reports taking warfarin as prescribed by his primary care physician for the past three months. His INR is found to be elevated at 7.8 and he has active bleeding from a small laceration on his leg. The patient reports no recent changes in his diet or medication regimen. The patient's blood pressure is stable, but he has a decreased hemoglobin level of 8g/dL. What is the initial therapeutic step?

A 58-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with hematemesis and melena. He reports a sudden onset of abdominal pain and weakness. Vital signs reveal tachycardia, hypotension, and a decreased level of consciousness. A presumptive diagnosis of acute variceal hemorrhage is made. Which of these is the first step in management?
A 14-year-old boy presents with a raindrop-like rash on his arms and trunk. His parents report that he had a cough last week. Which one of these is the most common form of this condition?
What is the most common type of carcinoma in the stomach?

A 55-year-old male presents to the clinic with a complaint of chest pain and shortness of breath. He reports a history of hypertension and a family history of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Physical examination reveals a systolic ejection murmur and left ventricular septal hypertrophy on echocardiography. Which of these interventions will most likely prevent SCD in this patient?

A 24-year-old male presents to the emergency with chest pain and shortness of breath for the last 24 hours. He says it has worsened rapidly and is now even present at a rest. Past history is unremarkable except for an upper respiratory tract infection 4 days ago. An urgent EKG is performed which is unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of these best establishes a diagnosis of asthma?

answers.option: PFTs before and after a bronchodilator

question: Which one of these is the best diagnostic test for bacterial overgrowth syndrome?

A 15-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with the complaint of generalized itching all over his body, which developed after eating a dessert made by his friend. He is a known case of peanut allergy. Vitals are stable, and physical examination is unremarkable for any sign of respiratory distress or mucocutaneous swellling. Which of the following diagnosis and treatment combinations are most appropriate for this case?
Which one of these treatment options is the first line for mitral stenosis with significant symptoms?
A 23-year-old primigravida, at 28 weeks of gestation, presents with shortness of breath. On examination, she has a loud S1 and an erratic pulse. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 29-year-old female presents to the office with complaints of dry eyes, mouth, and loose stools for the last few months. Which one of the following disease combinations best describes her condition?
A 59-year-old male, a known case of squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus, presents with new-onset coughing every time he consumes a meal. What complication has he most likely developed?

answers.option: Fistula between esophagus and bronchial tree
